newsitem.title: USA: Hilton Q3 gaming cash flow rises 62 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hilton Q3 gaming cash flow rises 62 pct.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp on Tuesday said third quarter earnings were bolstered by solid results from its hotel division and operations in Las Vegas that led to a 62 percent rise in gaming cash flow.
The gaming division saw its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), or cash flow, rise to $65.9 million from $40.8 million one year ago.

Though Las Vegas operations were strong, results at Hilton's two Reno, Nev. hotel/casinos continued to be hurt by competition and a soft market. Also, the Flamingo Hilton in Laughlin, Nev. was hurt by sluggish market conditions.
Australian casinos also had strong results, Hilton said.

Cash flow for the hotel division was $95.9 million, a 48 percent rise from $64.8 million a year ago. Hlton's 10 major owned and partially owned properties in New York, Honolulu, Chicago and other cities were primarily responsible. The 10 hotels showed 82 percent occupancy versus 81 percent in 1995 and an average daily rate of $144 vs. $133 last year.
Overall occupancy for Hilton's hotel division rose to 77 percent from 76 percent last year with average daily rate improving eight percent to $129.

"Our outstanding third-quarter results demonstrate the pricing power inherent in owning large full-service hotels such as The Waldorf-Astoria and Hilton Hawaiian Village, as well as the strength of our core Las Vegas gaming operations," Stephen Bollenbach, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Earlier, Hilton reported net income of $54.5 million, or $0.28 a share, beating analysts estimates of about $0.23 a share, adjusted for a recent four-for-one stock split.
In 1995's third quarter, Hilton earned $24.8 million, or $0.13 a share, adjusted for the split.
Hilton shares were off 1/8 at 28-1/8 by mid-morning.
